evidence_span.text: In the present study, we performed in vivo time-lapse imaging of cerebral capillary network formation in zebrafish. We show that sprouting tip cells undergo two distinct phases: a non-directional phase and a directional phase, in which they exhibit different cellular behaviors. Cxcr4a and Cxcl12b are important for inducing the phase transition to the directional phase, thereby promoting directional migration toward the anastomotic target.

reviews.rationale: Cxcr4a perturbation supports its role in directional tip-cell migration during cerebral capillary formation. The brain endothelial setting is relevant, but the species and developmental stage differ from the target context.

evidence_span.text: In summary, these data identified an angiogenesis defect with clustered IB4-positive EC as well as activated, clustered microglia in Tgfbr2-cKO.

reviews.rationale: Neural Tgfbr2 deletion causally impairs embryonic brain angiogenesis through altered paracrine signaling. This supports the regulator-level mechanism but does not investigate either supplied gene assigned to mechanism 3.

evidence_span.text: Organoid morphogenesis models revealed abnormal cessation of proliferation, abnormalities in expression of tip and stalk genes, and a failure to properly form elongating tubes. These defects were influenced by both hyperactive PI-3' kinase signaling and altered TGF-β signaling.

reviews.rationale: The paper links altered TGF-beta signaling to abnormal tip/stalk programs and tube morphogenesis, but the signaling direction and specific receptor contribution are unresolved. The pathological vascular-malformation context is related but not equivalent to normal postnatal development.

evidence_span.text: The functional downregulation of endothelial Kir2.1 using dominant-negative Kir2.1 construct resulted in substantial reductions in the response to flow in mesenteric arteries of lean mice, whereas no effect was observed in arteries of obese mice. Overexpressing wild-type-Kir2.1 in endothelium of arteries from obese mice resulted in full recovery of the flow response.

reviews.rationale: Gene-specific loss- and gain-of-function experiments establish endothelial Kir2.1 as a mediator of arterial flow responses. The study uses mesenteric arteries and an obesity setting rather than developing brain endothelium.
